title: Submit button disabled when first name is empty
gherkin:
Feature: Registration mandatory fields validation
  Scenario: Submit button remains disabled when first name is empty
    Given the registration form is displayed
    And the last name field is filled with "Smith"
    And the email field is filled with "user@example.com"
    And the phone number field is filled with "1234567890"
    And the password field is filled with "SecurePass123"
    And the legal consent checkbox is checked
    When the first name field is left empty
    Then the Submit button should be disabled
rationale: Validates that first name is a mandatory field and the Submit button remains disabled until it is filled. This directly tests the core requirement that all mandatory fields must be filled before submission.
usedContextItems: All mandatory fields must be filled before Submit button is enabled|All fields are mandatory and must be validated before submission
generationSummary: Test suite for R1 (Registration mandatory fields) validates that all mandatory fields must be completed and the legal consent checkbox must be checked before the Submit button is enabled. Tests cover individual field validation, combined field validation, checkbox requirement, and the critical conflict regarding phone number optionality (JIRA-Auth-114 vs. primary requirement). Tests also address the gap identified in E6 regarding separate checkboxes for Terms of Service and Privacy Policy compliance.
resolvedOperativeContext: Submit button remains disabled until all mandatory fields are filled and the legal consent checkbox is checked || Registration form includes a single 'Terms and Conditions' checkbox representing acceptance of both Terms of Service and Privacy Policy || All mandatory fields must be filled before Submit button is enabled || All fields are mandatory and must be validated before submission.
resolvedConflictsOrObsolete: JIRA-Auth-114 proposes making phone number optional, which conflicts with the primary requirement that phone number is mandatory
resolutionNotes: E6 (Legal compliance email) signals a release-blocking requirement that the current single checkbox design violates; separate checkboxes for Terms of Service and Privacy Policy are required. E8 and E9 contain conflicting requirements: E8 proposes optional phone number while E1 and primary evidence establish phone as mandatory. E5 and E7 refine validation rules. E10 provides broader authentication context. E11 confirms disabled submit button behavior. E12 documents the email uniqueness vs. multi-user contradiction that needs resolution. Filtered abstract or low-relevance operative statements: first name, last name, phone number, email address, and password | First name and last name are separate fields, each limited to 50 characters | Leading and trailing spaces in name fields are trimmed; hyphens and accents are allowed
